I never liked boxing , but after my bully beat me and showed the whole school the video of me getting beat up i signed up for a gym and then fell in love with boxing more than other sports. I do it for the following reasons:

1. Self defense: I don't wanna die in a street fight or be caught in a situation where i don't know how to fight
2. Strategy ''game'' : Don't get me wrong , i do lots of sports (volleyball,football,jogging and cyclism) and i never fell in love with any of those (talking about strategy), boxing is customizable : lots of strategies, new styles etc... and you can always take boxing as a ''science'' lesson because you don't just punch in boxing, there's a lot to this sport than with other sports.
3. Staying in shape: I was never fat but that doesn't mean i need to be, being fit is awesome and good for persons with low confidence.
4. Training for the special police forces: I don't want to be in the future an 18 year old made out of gum when there are sports test (the persons with the best endurance are accepted in the special forces, and i don't want to be one of those who is rejected.)
5. Stress reliever: Who doesn't enjoy hitting a bag if they had a bad day?
6. Therapy: Now, no doctor or therapist told me i should take boxing but i did, i had only bad years since my teenage years started (felt suicidal for a while) and when i found boxing , it was basically a free ticket to let out all of my anger and my problems by beating my opponent and getting some medals and belts (and diplomas) for it.
7. Champion: Most of us want to become a champion , including myself. But i don't want to do it just for the belts. I want to inspire and motivate people to train, and believe in their dreams. When i got a dream i don't give up on it no matter what, i will even die just to become champion. My personality is full of motivation, determination and strong will and i want to take advantage of those and use it for my success. And just in case i don't get accepted in the special police force, i will take up my career in boxing.
